equity.level_reason: The analysis stratifies only by region and age, with no social-position framing of the age results; race/ethnicity and health inequities are raised only in the conclusions as background and a recommendation to prioritize equity.

equity.equity_measurement: No race/ethnicity or socioeconomic data were analysed; the authors cite 'limited covariate data', and the equity statement rests on an external CDC data page.

notes: Stratified pre/post comparisons by region and age are explicitly labelled stratified, so the depth is stratified/adjusted; the Pearson correlation is the only computed estimate and carries no test or CI. Percent changes and baseline ratios are arithmetic, not procedures. [review] Agree with the structural record: pre/post comparisons within region and age group meet stratified depth, and region-day correlation with PM2.5 is an ecologic time-series reading. Extreme weather is an environmental exposure, not a social determinant.
view_issues: The Preliminary Conclusions call the Eastern Lake Ontario (179.1%) and Central (132.8%) increases 'twofold', which understates the reported increases (about 2.8-fold and 2.3-fold).
